science.claim: Sound in air at approximately 20C travels at approximately 343 m/s
science.working: Independent real fact, not a justification for the fantasy sound-storage rule. NPL primary PDF verified by the parent (see evidence/science-preflight.json): calculation 331.3 + 0.606 * 20 gives 343.42 m/s, rounded to 343 m/s for air at approximately 20C. Speed varies with conditions. The narration says 'approximately' ('rao').
science.source: NPL primary PDF, verified by parent; evidence file: evidence/science-preflight.json

science.claim: Touching an object silences it, and ALL stored sounds return together immediately when the protagonist laughs
science.working: Sole fictional rule of this episode (fantasy sound storage). Not physics, no scientific basis; must never be drawn on the science schematic as fact. The narrative consequence ('a stored horn does not wait for the protagonist to choose the moment') follows this rule only.
science.source: None - fictional premise of the episode

translation_en: Tap your alarm. Quiet. Tap the jackhammer. Quiet. Tap the truck horn. Quiet. The truck keeps coming. What if one tap silenced anything, and all stored sounds return when you laugh? In air at 20 degrees Celsius, sound moves at about 343 metres a second. That's real. How long can you hold a laugh?

notes_for_review: YouTube collision: the parent found the generic premise 'What If You Could Silence Any Sound?' plus many mute-people/mute-things episodes; the generic premise is rejected. The parent chose the laughter-return twist as the differentiator, but it is NOT proven globally unique. The old touch-again restoration rule is fully superseded and removed everywhere. Only objects are muted; muting a horn does not silence the street; no person is ever muted. Step 1 only: no shots, edit, fx or sound events yet. No audio generated, no oral listening has occurred, actual duration unmeasured (target 15-25 s only). Parent submits all paid requests after QC.
